clue.text: There'll be trouble brewing if the workers go on strike there

definitions.text: There'll be trouble brewing if the workers go on strike there

parts.words: There'll be trouble brewing if the workers go on strike there
parts.note: a strike in a famous brewing town would literally stop the beer brewing, while 'trouble brewing' also means trouble coming

explanation.surface: A warning that industrial action at some workplace will cause unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: Burton upon Trent, in the English Midlands, is Britain's best-known brewing town, so a strike there means trouble for the brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Staffordshire town is famous for its breweries, the place where a strike would halt beer production.

clue.text: Rings up about my going over Indian territory?

indicators.note: in a down clue the word my sits over, above, the rest of the pieces

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are written upward, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: O is a ring, so rings are OS
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone telephoning about a border dispute over a stretch of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rings up' looks like making a phone call; here 'up' turns OS into SO in this down entry, and 'going over' places MY at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysore was a princely state of southern India, now part of Karnataka.

clue.text: The man in charge of the military exercises

definitions.text: The man in charge of the military exercises

parts.words: The man in charge of the military exercises
parts.note: military exercises on the parade ground are drills, and the person running them trains recruits

explanation.surface: A description of an officer commanding a military manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant who trains recruits in marching and parade-ground routines is given this title.

clue.text: Trust broken by a girl rising promptly?

indicators.note: the word for trust is split open so the other piece can sit inside it

parts.note: to rely on someone is to trust them

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the piece is written upward, reading backwards

parts.note: Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Faith shattered by a young woman getting up quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The lone 'a' is a link word; 'rising' turns the girl's name upward in this down entry before 'broken by' splits the trust word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something readily means doing it at once and without hesitation.

clue.text: The type of people who unfortunately have very little in common

definitions.text: The type of people who unfortunately have very little in common

parts.words: The type of people who unfortunately have very little in common
parts.note: reads as people who share few interests, but 'have very little' means they are poor

explanation.surface: A remark about a group of people who share no interests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have very little in common' suggests few shared interests; the real sense is that they all own very little.
explanation.definitionFit: The deprived and poor lack the advantages and wealth that others enjoy.

clue.text: Printed material, non-obtainable in a Mediterranean island

annotationWithheld.why: Printed material, non-obtainable in a Mediterranean island (8): CRETE holds ONN, and no fair reading of 'non-obtainable' gives ONN without a missing indicator or a misprint
annotationWithheld.clue: Printed material, non-obtainable in a Mediterranean island

clue.text: Allow a penalty perhaps

explanation.surface: Permitting a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to authorise; a sanction is also a punitive measure such as a trade embargo.

clue.text: Cheapest way to get drinks when on holiday?

definitions.text: Cheapest way to get drinks when on holiday?

parts.words: Cheapest way to get drinks when on holiday?
parts.note: travellers buying spirits at the airport shop pay no excise tax on them

explanation.surface: Tips for saving money on alcohol while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold at airports without excise or import tax are cheaper for travellers.

clue.text: Usual standard followed by a learner

indicators.note: the standard comes first and the other pieces follow it

parts.note: a norm is a standard
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A typical benchmark trailed by a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something normal is ordinary, what one would expect.

clue.text: A divine increase

parts.note: a divine is a clergyman, and DD is a Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A heavenly growth.
explanation.definitionFit: To add is to make larger by putting more on.

clue.text: Walked a little way, then turned over?

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way in little
something rolled has turned over

explanation.surface: Someone who walked a short distance and then rolled over.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroll is to walk at a leisurely pace.

clue.text: Offer the wrong type of inducement

definitions.text: Offer the wrong type of inducement

parts.words: Offer the wrong type of inducement
parts.note: to tempt someone, often into doing wrong, by holding out a reward or attraction

explanation.surface: Advice against using an unsuitable incentive.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone with promises, frequently towards wrongdoing.

clue.text: It gives an impression of permanence

definitions.text: It gives an impression of permanence

parts.words: It gives an impression of permanence
parts.note: 'impression' is the mark a writing tool makes, and this mark cannot be rubbed out

explanation.surface: Something that makes things look as though they will last.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil whose graphite contains dye, so its writing cannot be erased.

clue.text: An act of duplicity?

parts.note: duplicity is taken as doubleness, and an act is a stage turn performed by two people

explanation.surface: A deceitful deed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of performers working together form a double act.

clue.text: The skill shown when the War Office turns in papers

indicators.note: the War Office piece is placed inside the word for papers

parts.note: the press means newspapers collectively

indicators.note: turns tells us the War Office abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: WO is the abbreviation for the War Office

explanation.surface: Military expertise revealed when a government department appears in the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Prowess is great ability or expertise, as in battle.

clue.text: Eloquent turn of phrase

parts.note: persuasive, often showy language used to impress an audience

explanation.surface: A well-spoken expression.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of persuasive speaking or writing, or language designed to impress.

clue.text: Dingoes for the gods?

parts.note: the letters of the word dogs, rearranged (made wild), spell gods

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Australian dogs are meant for the deities.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: shake up DOGS ('wild' as an anagram signal) and you get GODS, the word in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Dingoes are Australia's feral canines.

clue.text: Those birds in the loft George points out?

definitions.text: Those birds in the loft George points out?

parts.words: Those birds in the loft George points out?
parts.note: a fancier showing a visitor the racing birds kept in a loft above the house

explanation.surface: A man indicating the birds kept up in his loft.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds kept in a loft are racing or homing doves.

clue.text: Very colourful Japanese ladies' band

parts.note: band means a sash, not a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A vivid all-female pop group from Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a music group; it is the broad sash worn with a kimono.
explanation.definitionFit: The wide sash tied round a kimono is often brightly coloured.

clue.text: Not in favour of the jingles on commercial television?

indicators.note: in a down entry, the jingles sit on top of the advert word only in the surface; here on places the verse piece after it

parts.note: an ad is what commercial television broadcasts
advertising jingles are light verse

explanation.surface: Disliking the catchy tunes played in television commercials.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions are hostile, working against one.

clue.text: Admittedly lost as a soldier

parts.note: 'admittedly' is read as officially stated, the status of a soldier who cannot be found after action

explanation.surface: A confession of having lost one's way while in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers who cannot be accounted for after battle are officially listed as absent.

clue.text: Upper class student in sore distress

indicators.note: distress here means damage or disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A privileged scholar in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upper class' is not social class: in an American school the top year's class is the most advanced one.
explanation.definitionFit: In US schools and colleges a student in the final year belongs to the highest class.

clue.text: I haphazardly turn over a valuable fur

indicators.note: haphazardly means randomly, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flipping over a precious pelt at random.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link word: shuffling I and TURN gives NUTRI, followed by A.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutria is the pelt of the coypu, a South American rodent farmed for fur.

clue.text: Knotted cord in from Scandinavia

indicators.note: knotted string is tangled, so these letters are tied up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tangled rope brought in from northern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Nordic describes the peoples and countries of northern Europe such as Norway and Sweden.

clue.text: No end of time

parts.note: read not as 'lots of time' but as time that never finishes

explanation.surface: An expression meaning a great deal of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinite duration, time without any close.

clue.text: A hot spread on the way?

definitions.text: A hot spread on the way?

parts.words: A hot spread on the way?
parts.note: sounds like a warm meal being delivered, but the spread is a road surface laid while hot

explanation.surface: A warm buffet that is coming soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Heated pitch is laid on roads as a surface.

clue.text: Serenade? Wrong note as well we hear

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
G is a musical note

indicators.note: we hear tells us the piece is a word that sounds the same as another spelling

parts.note: too means as well

explanation.surface: Asking whether a serenade with a false note counts, as rumoured.
explanation.definitionFit: To serenade someone is to perform songs for them, as a lover under a balcony.

clue.text: Make haste to get on a bus or train, maybe.

definitions.text: to get on a bus or train, maybe

explanation.surface: Hurry to board public transport.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means hurry up; literally it is placing a foot on the vehicle to board.
